INDEPENDENT WEBSITE BUILDBOUTIQUE HOTEL

Slow Morning House

A boutique hotel website with room comparison, guest-capacity checks and a stay estimate including optional breakfast.

My role: Website design & frontend development

ROOMSSTAY COMPARISONLOCAL GUIDE
Read case study+

Company

Slow Morning House is a boutique hotel brand built around considered rooms and a quieter city stay. I designed and developed its website to connect room comparison with dates, guest count, optional breakfast and a sample stay estimate.

Market / Customer

Travellers comparing rooms and planning a stay for a specific group and date range.

Problem

Guests need to compare room capacity, stay length and extras before choosing the right accommodation.

Product / Service

Three room options, date and guest inputs, room comparison, capacity feedback, optional breakfast and calculated sample totals. The hotel model shown is room-night pricing with an optional breakfast add-on. The build supports stay planning with sample rates.

Business Goal

Make room selection and the estimated cost of a stay easy to understand.

My Role

Website design & frontend development.

Work

I created the hotel identity, responsive room presentation, stay planner, date validation, guest-capacity feedback and pricing calculations.

Solution

Room characteristics and planner inputs share one estimate, making the effect of nights, guests and breakfast visible.

Outcome

A working three-room comparison and stay calculator with validation and capacity feedback. It does not check live availability or create reservations.

Scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.

INDEPENDENT WEBSITE BUILDRESIDENTIAL ESTATE AGENCY

Good Neighbour Homes

A property website combining home profiles, budget and area filters, saved shortlists and side-by-side comparison.

My role: Website design & frontend development

LISTINGSFILTERSSHORTLIST COMPARISON
Read case study+

Company

Good Neighbour Homes is a residential property brand organised around finding and comparing homes. I designed and developed a search experience that connects detailed listings, budget and area filters, a saved shortlist and a comparison view.

Market / Customer

Homebuyers narrowing a search by location, property type, budget and practical living requirements.

Problem

Comparing listings across separate pages makes it harder to remember trade-offs in price, space and location.

Product / Service

Illustrative home profiles and detail dialogs, area/type/budget filters, list and map views, locally saved homes and comparison of up to three properties. The agency model shown is property discovery leading toward a viewing enquiry. The build covers search and comparison with sample listings.

Business Goal

Help buyers narrow options and compare the details that matter before a viewing.

My Role

Website design & frontend development.

Work

I built the blue and white property identity, listing views, filters, detail dialogs, local-storage shortlist, comparison table and arithmetic budget estimator.

Solution

One set of listing data feeds browsing, saved homes and comparison, keeping the decision process connected.

Outcome

Working filters, property details, an illustrative map, saved shortlists and comparison of up to three homes. Listings are sample data; there is no listing feed or viewing pipeline.

Scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.

INDEPENDENT WEBSITE BUILDBOTANICAL HAIR-CARE BRAND

Root Ritual

A hair-care website presenting three oil products and a routine matcher that connects hair preferences to product use.

My role: Website design & frontend development

THREE OILSINGREDIENTSROUTINE MATCHER
Read case study+

Company

Root Ritual is a botanical hair-care brand organised around everyday finishing, pre-wash scalp care and lightweight care for ends. I designed and built its product-discovery website, pairing a three-product collection with an interactive routine matcher.

Market / Customer

Hair-care shoppers comparing product purposes and deciding where an oil fits into an existing routine.

Problem

A product collection needs to explain differences in use, size and routine placement before a shopper can choose.

Product / Service

Everyday Hair Oil, Pre-Wash Scalp Oil and Ends & Shine Oil each have selectable detail views. Hair-feel and care-timing choices produce a matching routine and product link. The brand model shown is a consumer hair-care range discovered through product education. The delivered website covers discovery rather than transactions.

Business Goal

Make each product purpose clear and connect the collection to a simple care routine.

My Role

Website design & frontend development.

Work

I developed a centred botanical product campaign, an open three-oil collection, detailed product states and preference-based routine matching in JavaScript.

Solution

A collection-first boutique layout leads from the central bottle campaign into product comparison and a matching care routine; ingredient information reads as a botanical notebook.

Outcome

Three working product views and a routine matcher with nine preference combinations. Product formulas and usage copy are illustrative; no checkout is implemented.

Scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.

My role: Website design & frontend development

SEASONAL MENUDIETARY FILTERSPICKUP BASKET

Company

The Sunday Table is a neighbourhood restaurant brand centred on seasonal plates and shared meals. I designed and developed a website that joins menu discovery, dietary filtering, meal planning and a local pickup basket.

Market / Customer

Diners planning a shared meal and people choosing dishes for collection.

Problem

Diners need to compare dishes, dietary information, quantities and estimated spend before deciding what to order.

Product / Service

Dinner, lunch and drinks views, a meat-and-fish filter, item quantities and totals, a four-dish sharing plan and date-based table-time suggestions. Website design & frontend development.

I created the bistro identity and responsive menu, implemented dietary/category filters and built the basket, quantity controls, totals and table-time suggestions.

Solution

Browsing, dietary preferences and quantities stay connected, so the basket reflects the meal a visitor has chosen.

Outcome

A working menu and basket with changing quantities and totals, plus meal and table-time planning. No order or table reservation is submitted.

INDEPENDENT WEBSITE BUILDBARBERSHOP

Good Form Barbers

A barbershop website connecting five grooming services, barber profiles, a visit planner and practical aftercare.

My role: Website design & frontend development

SERVICE MENUBARBERSAFTERCARE
Read case study+

Company

Good Form Barbers is a barbershop brand built around tailored cuts, beard care and time in the chair. I designed and developed a service-led website that helps visitors compare treatments, plan a visit and find relevant aftercare.

Market / Customer

People choosing a haircut or beard service and comparing the time, price and style of a visit.

Problem

Visitors need enough service detail to choose a treatment and understand the visit before committing to an appointment.

Product / Service

Five service descriptions, three barber profiles, a service/barber/day/time planner and a style-specific aftercare selector. The service model shown is appointment-based grooming with defined durations and sample prices.

Make service selection clear and reduce the information needed to plan a visit.

Website design & frontend development.

Work

I built the charcoal and rose visual system, responsive service layouts, visit summary and short-cut, beard and longer-texture aftercare states.

Solution

Service, barber and time choices update one visit summary, while aftercare extends the customer journey beyond the selection.

A working visit planner and three aftercare guides. The planner displays sample appointments and does not request or reserve a slot.

INDEPENDENT WEBSITE BUILDVETERINARY PRACTICE

Kindred Vet

A veterinary website helping pet owners choose a visit reason, prepare questions and download a private visit note.

My role: Website design & frontend development

CARE GUIDEVISIT NOTESPREPARATION
Read case study+

Company

Kindred Vet is a veterinary practice brand focused on clear guidance and calmer visits for pets and their owners. I designed and built a website that explains care categories and helps owners prepare a visit note they can take to a veterinary team.

Market / Customer

Pet owners organising routine care, preventive visits or questions about a new concern.

Problem

Owners need to understand the next step and collect relevant questions and observations before a veterinary conversation.

Product / Service

Pet-species and visit-reason selectors, preparation guidance, service categories, common questions and a downloadable text note for observations, medicines and questions. The practice model shown is appointment-based veterinary care. The delivered product supports visit preparation and information organisation.

Business Goal

Help owners arrive with clear observations and questions, supporting a more organised conversation.

My Role

Website design & frontend development.

Work

I developed a compact care-planning portal, species/reason guidance, service-information panels and private note creation with text-file download.

Solution

The pet and visit-reason choices are available immediately, with preparation guidance beside them. A notebook-style form keeps observations and questions in the current tab until the owner chooses to download them.

Outcome

A working guidance selector and downloadable visit note. The website does not book visits, diagnose conditions or transmit clinical records.

Scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.

INDEPENDENT WEBSITE BUILDCUSTOM FURNITURE BRAND

Honest Grain

A furniture website turning piece, size, wood and finish choices into a copyable design brief.

My role: Website design & frontend development

FURNITURECONFIGURATORDESIGN BRIEF
Read case study+

Company

Honest Grain is a furniture brand organised around material choice, useful proportions and custom pieces. I designed and built a website that connects product specifications with a configurator and a clear brief for a prospective commission.

Market / Customer

People considering furniture for a space and comparing dimensions, material and finish.

Problem

Custom-furniture enquiries need a clear specification before a maker can discuss feasibility and price.

Product / Service

Three furniture pieces, dimension controls, material and finish choices, specification updates and a copyable design brief. The maker model shown is made-to-order furniture discussed through a project brief. The build prepares that brief without submitting an order or quote request.

Business Goal

Turn product interest into a clear specification for a commissioning conversation.

My Role

Website design & frontend development.

Work

I created the measured furniture identity, product/specification views, dimension constraints and configurator, including clipboard copying and an availability message when copying is unavailable.

Solution

The configurator keeps the chosen piece and its options together, then translates them into a concise brief the visitor can reuse.

Outcome

A working three-piece configurator and clipboard-copy action. Specifications stay visible if copying is unavailable. No quote, manufacturing order or request is sent.

Scope: Independent frontend build. Business details are illustrative; interactions run in the browser.

Company

First Whistle Academy is a youth football academy brand organised around age-group coaching for U7–U16 players. I designed and built its website to connect programme selection, training information and first-session preparation in one clear journey.

Market / Customer

Parents and guardians comparing training options, and young players preparing to join an age-appropriate group.

Problem

Families need to understand the coaching focus, session format and practical preparation before choosing a programme.

Product / Service

Three age-group views show coaching priorities, session length and sample schedules. A kit checklist and first-session guide turn interest into practical preparation. The academy model shown is scheduled age-group coaching, supported by programme information and an introductory session journey.

Business Goal

Help families identify the right programme and arrive prepared for a first session.

My Role

Website design & frontend development.

Work

I created the athletic website identity, responsive page structure, age-group selector, changing programme details and interactive kit checklist.

Solution

Programme content follows the family decision process: choose an age group, understand the training, then prepare for the first visit.

Outcome

A responsive website with three working programme states and a four-item checklist. Enrolment and trial booking are outside the delivered scope.
